new_statements.quote: Ces faits semblent justifier l’adoption du trochée comme pied de base en LSQ. Il peut prendre la forme d’un trochée morique (pied contenant deux mores, soit dans la même syllabe longue, soit dans deux syllabes courtes: σµµ ou σµ σµ), d’un trochée syllabique léger (σµ σµ) ou d’un trochée syllabique lourd (σµµ σµµ). À la différence du trochée, l’iambe joue un rôle restreint en LSQ. Deux classes de signes ont une forme iambique: les composés (dont le premier signe est normalement réduit) et certaines formes emphatiques. La plupart des signes à plus d’une syllabe prennent la forme d’un trochée.
new_statements.translation: These facts seem to justify adopting the trochee as the basic foot in LSQ. It can take the form of a moraic trochee (a foot containing two moras, either in the same long syllable or in two short syllables: σµµ or σµ σµ), a light syllabic trochee (σµ σµ) or a heavy syllabic trochee (σµµ σµµ). Unlike the trochee, the iamb plays a restricted role in LSQ. Two classes of signs have an iambic form: compounds (whose first sign is normally reduced) and certain emphatic forms. Most signs of more than one syllable take the form of a trochee.
new_statements.citation: Miller, Christopher. 2000. Regards sur la phonologie des langues signées. Recherches linguistiques de Vincennes 29: 101-120. doi:10.4000/rlv.1201
new_statements.locator: §5.2.2 'Une représentation métrique pour la LSQ', pp. 112-113

À la différence du trochée, l'iambe joue un rôle restreint en LSQ. Deux classes de signes…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sign-language analogue of word stress: LSQ signs are parsed into trochaic (left-headed) feet, so in a polysyllabic (in practice disyllabic) sign the metrically strong syllable/movement is the first; compounds (with reduced first member) and some emphatic forms are right-headed (iambic). A minimal isolated sign = one moraic trochee (one long movement or two short ones).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed at word level; higher metrical constituents are built cyclically up to a single phrasal accent, and repetition/reduplication of short (monomoraic) movements is conditioned by the surrounding metrical and syntactic structure (pp. 113-116); phrase-final threefold repetition is treated as final lengthening (p. 111).
new_statements.exceptions: Iambic (final-headed) form in compounds whose first sign is reduced and in certain emphatic forms; signs made of heterogeneous syllable sequences are limited to two syllables and most polysyllabic signs are repetitions of one base syllable (p. 113); degenerate foot = a lone monomoraic syllable, repaired by reduplication or by grouping with an adjacent degenerate foot unless a major syntactic boundary intervenes.
new_statements.domain_note: This is a sign language: 'stress' here is metrical headedness of movement syllables within the sign (phonological word), argued from minimal-sign size and alignment of head-nod non-manuals with syllable/mora structure, within Hayes (1985/1995) metrical theory explicitly framed as the theory of 'accent tonique'. The author does not give phonetic correlates of the foot head in this article. Data are from LSQ phrasal (connected-discourse) contexts as well as isolated signs. The mapping onto the spoken-language category 'fixed: initial syllable' is my provisional reading of 'trochee = basic foot; most polysyllabic signs are trochees'.
new_statements.identity_note: Quebec Sign Language (LSQ, queb1245, ISO fcs) is a sign language; the quoted statement concerns metrical foot structure/headedness of movement syllables within signs, the modality's analogue of word stress, not acoustic stress. Miller's data are from Montréal LSQ signers (UQAM corpus). Whether a sign-language metrical statement belongs in a word-stress catalog is a policy decision for the catalog owner; the earlier scan's 'inapplicable' classification is defensible, but a first-hand published statement does exist.

sources.quote: Ces faits semblent justifier l’adoption du trochée comme pied de base en LSQ. Il peut prendre la forme d’un trochée morique (pied contenant deux mores, soit dans la même syllabe longue, soit dans deux syllabes courtes: σµµ ou σµ σµ), d’un trochée syllabique léger (σµ σµ) ou d’un trochée syllabique lourd (σµµ σµµ). sources.locator: §5.2.2 'Une représentation métrique pour la LSQ', pp. 112-113
sources.note: §5.2 applies Hayes-style metrical theory to LSQ: the trochee is the basic foot of LSQ; most signs of more than one syllable are trochaic (head = first syllable); the iamb is restricted to compounds (first sign reduced) and certain emphatic forms; heterogeneous syllable sequences are limited to two syllables; degenerate foot = monomoraic syllable; repetition of short movements is governed by rhythmic/metrical structure and phrase-final lengthening (pp. 111-116).
